1.name: Protect
1.short: The nerve is inflamed. The work is protection, not effort.
1.body: Nothing you do with the muscle will speed the nerve up in this stage, and pushing hard can make things harder later. So the programme is deliberately quiet: protect the eye, keep the tissue supple, support the resting position of the face, and let the inflammation settle.
1.tapeMode: Resting support — lifts the mid-face against gravity. No pull into movement.

2.name: Activate
2.short: The first signals are arriving. We help the brain find them.
2.window: Usually weeks 2–6, once any flicker of movement appears
2.body: A flicker is enough to work with. The goal now is to find the smallest movement you can actually produce and repeat it accurately, rather than to produce a big movement badly. Small and correct beats large and recruited.

avoid.a1: Effortful straining, which recruits the wrong muscles
avoid.a2: Long sets — fatigue makes the pattern worse

2.tapeMode: Assist — tape helps the movement you are trying to make, so less effort is needed.

3.name: Coordination
3.short: Movement exists. Now it needs to go where you send it.
3.body: At this stage most people can produce movement but not isolate it — the eye narrows when you smile, or the corner of the mouth pulls when you close the eye. Coordination work teaches separation. This is slower and less satisfying than strength work, and it matters more.

focus.f1: Separating eye movement from mouth movement
focus.f2: Slow, controlled range through the middle of movement
focus.f3: Holding a position rather than snapping to it

avoid.a2: Practising the linked pattern you are trying to unlearn
avoid.a3: Working past the point of fatigue

3.tapeMode: Guide — tape gives a directional cue and discourages the linked movement.

4.name: Refine
4.short: The face works. We are after control at low effort.
4.body: Refinement is about the movements you use without thinking: speaking, eating, expressions in conversation. The exercises get closer to real life and further from the mirror, and tension management becomes as important as activation.

focus.f2: Symmetry at conversational effort, not maximum effort

avoid.a2: Ignoring tightness because movement is present

4.tapeMode: Occasional — used for specific tasks or tiredness, not daily.

5.name: Maintain
5.short: Holding what you have built, and using it.
5.body: Recovery flattens out but does not usually reverse. A shorter maintenance routine protects range and keeps tightness from creeping back, with periodic scans so any drift is caught early rather than discovered late.

avoid.a1: Stopping entirely and losing range quietly

5.tapeMode: Not routine. Available for tiring days or specific events.
